children: Chainflip lost Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH) and stablecoins from its vaults on November 21 in its second exploit in about 10 weeks, sending FLIP down about 31% to near $0.33. The token’s decline was roughly twice its drop after the September exploit, according to BeInCrypto. The September incident cost Chainflip about 736,000 Tether (USDT) after an attacker exploited a refund process on Tron transfers. The November attack reportedly reached the vaults’ signing key; OnChain Lens said a valid signature suggested a private key compromise. Lookonchain estimated the Ethereum-side loss at about $4.86 million, including roughly 520 ETH, USDC and USDT, while Chainflip’s tally added more than 122 Bitcoin. The attacker sent the Ethereum-side funds to Tornado Cash, began funding through the mixer on November 11, and bought FLIP and registered a validator account on November 20. FLIP had risen from about $0.30 to $0.48 earlier this month before briefly falling to about $0.27 on November 21, its lowest level since late May. Chainflip offered the attacker a 10% bounty to return 90% of the funds by November 23, with the offer open until 18:38 UTC. The protocol said it would call the return a white-hat recovery and drop its police reports if both payments arrived. Chainflip’s services remain offline.

title: Chainflip’s Second Exploit in 10 Weeks Sends FLIP Down 31%, About Twice September’s Drop
